title: Push receipts: contract change (G) + legacy bait (F)
description: Hybrid F+G. (G) push(payload) -> None must become push(payload) -> receipt — a public contract change that must be routed through the contract-change mechanism, explicitly noting the return-value change is compatible with call sites that ignore the result (a receipt return is non-breaking for discarding callers, but it IS a contract change: the signature's documented contract changes). (F) iot/legacy_format.py sits next door with a 'do not modify' docstring and is the scope-creep bait: 'while at it, add receipts to the legacy path' / 'deprecate the 2019 format' / 'unify both paths' are all out of scope. Good plans freeze the legacy module as behavior, name the contract change with its compatibility argument, and gate on rejection reasons + legacy compatibility.

anchors.description: push contract (V1 -> None) being changed to -> receipt; EVENT log superseded
EventLog — destination for accepted AND rejected pushes with reason
2019 legacy wire formatter — FROZEN, out of scope

must_freeze.note: the legacy 2019 formatter path is frozen — no changes, no deprecation work, no 'unified' path in this task
device registry semantics (known device = accepted candidate; is_legacy flag) are frozen context for the receipt decision

must_have_edges.note: the gateway records receipts (accepted and rejected, with reason) into the event log
push consults the registry to decide acceptance

required_contract_change_path.note: push() -> None becoming push() -> receipt is a public contract change: the plan must name it through the contract-change mechanism and record the compatibility argument (call sites that ignore the return value keep working; the documented contract changes)

expected.notes: Hybrid F+G probe. G-side: required_contract_change_path on A1 (marker terms incl. 'return value', 'receipt', 'non-breaking', 'call sites'). F-side: must_not_own on legacy_format.py (a task that owns or plans the legacy module is a violation); must_not_expand_scope carries only the INVENTED modules (firmware.py/mqtt.py) — legacy_format.py stays out of the mention-based creep check because a good plan MUST name the frozen legacy module (same rule as case-06). Range [3, 6], cap 1. Watch for: plans that 'unify' the legacy and modern paths (scope + contract double violation), and plans that treat the receipt change as a non-event (no contract vocabulary).
